source_name: CEED Consulting — Montenegro business consultancy
why_relevant: Leading Montenegrin business-consulting firm explicitly serving banking clients; produces sector studies, feasibility work and SME surveys that occasionally quantify merchant acceptance and financing behaviour.

source_name: UBCG — Udruženje banaka Crne Gore, magazine 'Bankar'
why_relevant: The banking association's decade-old professional journal 'Bankar' carries semi-academic articles by bank practitioners and academics on payment systems, card business and digitalisation; issues are posted as full PDFs (e.g. Bankar 38).

source_name: CEEOL — Central and Eastern European Online Library (Montenegrin economics journals)
why_relevant: Aggregates full text of regional social-science journals including Montenegrin/Serbian publishers; the most efficient way to find local-language academic articles on payment behaviour that never surface in Google Scholar.

source_name: UDG — Univerzitet Donja Gorica, FIST / economics-finance faculties
why_relevant: Montenegro's main private university, with international-economics/finance and information-systems faculties (FIST) that supervise master theses on digital banking and payments; thesis rules and some works are posted on faculty subdomains.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala / SCMN — analytical publications (macroeconomic model of Montenegro)
why_relevant: The securities regulator hosts commissioned analytical studies (e.g. the ISSP-authored macroeconomic model of Montenegro PDF), showing that regulator sites act as republishers of think-tank analysis — a route to grey research not on the author's own site.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex 2025 — Montenegro demand-side financial-inclusion microdata
why_relevant: The only internationally comparable demand-side survey covering account ownership, digital payments, card use and cash reliance; Montenegro is among the 141 economies in the 2025 round (~145,000 adults). Microdata catalogue entry allows respondent-level analysis of cash-preference and digital-adoption for ME.

source_name: Visa 'Visa Pulse' regional consumer payment-habits research (Montenegro cut)
why_relevant: Scheme-commissioned consumer survey with Montenegro-specific figures (e.g. share of citizens buying online, share using smartphone as primary payment method) — exactly the cash-preference/digital-adoption metrics missing from official statistics. Full report is corporate; press coverage carries the numbers.

source_name: MONSTAT — Anketa o potrošnji domaćinstava (Household Budget Survey)
why_relevant: National household budget survey and its methodology/results releases are the standard denominator dataset that Montenegrin researchers use to model cash-intensive consumption categories; the survey instrument itself is the closest domestic analogue to a payment-habits survey.

source_name: Stellar Market Research — Montenegro Banking System Market (commercial syndicated report)
why_relevant: Example of the commercial syndicated-report layer covering Montenegro banking/payments (sizing and forecasts). Low methodological transparency but useful to map who sells ME-specific market reports and what they claim; comparable vendors (GlobalData 'Cards and Payments' series) publish per-country editions for regional peers.

source_name: TheBanks.eu — Montenegro banking sector structure and bank-level metrics
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator that reprocesses Montenegrin bank financial statements into comparable market-share, assets and loan-to-deposit metrics (e.g. 11 banks, CKB ~27.8% share, LTD ~85%). Useful analyst-layer baseline for sizing and for cross-checking domestic analyses.

source_name: CeJN - Elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore (portal javne nabavke, tenderi)
why_relevant: Current official Montenegrin e-procurement system. Contracting authorities (state bodies, municipalities, state-owned enterprises, Posta Crne Gore, EPCG, and the Central Bank itself) publish contract notices and awards here. Tenders for 'bankomati', 'POS terminali', 'kartice', 'termalne rolne', 'obrada kartichnih transakcija' and cash-handling equipment reveal demand, incumbent suppliers, contract values and renewal cycles that private-bank procurement never discloses.

source_name: Uprava/Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (Public Procurement Directorate) - ujn.gov.me
why_relevant: Regulator/administrator of the ME procurement system. Publishes the legal framework, annual reports on public procurement (aggregate volumes by CPV and authority), lists of contracting authorities, EU tender notices, and instructions that point to the correct portal(s). The annual report is a cheap way to size the ME public-sector market for payment/ATM-related categories.

source_name: eTender Portal UJN CG (legacy portal javnih nabavki, portalujn.gov.me)
why_relevant: Legacy Montenegrin procurement portal covering notices published under the pre-2020 Law on Public Procurement. Essential for historical baselines: previous ATM/POS/card-processing awards and which vendors won them before the CeJN migration. Search is explicitly open without registration.

source_name: eTenderi.me - commercial ME tender-alert aggregator with State Commission decision database
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that pushes SMS/email/push alerts on new ME tenders and, uniquely, offers OCR-searchable access to the full decision database of the State Commission for Control of Public Procurement Procedures (Komisija za kontrolu postupka javnih nabavki). Appeal decisions name bidders, prices and technical specs for ATM/POS lots that the notice itself omits - a rare weak-signal window into competitive dynamics.

source_name: Javne-nabavke.com - regional tender aggregator, Montenegro section
why_relevant: Regional (ex-YU) aggregator with a Montenegro feed and daily email alerts; useful for cross-border comparison of ATM/POS/card-processing procurement in ME vs RS/BA/HR and for catching notices from authorities not easily filtered on the official portal.

source_name: eKapija Tenderi - Montenegro public procurement, CPV-code search
why_relevant: Aggregator with explicit CPV-code search - the practical way to isolate ATM/POS/payment-terminal categories (e.g. CPV 30123000, 302xxxxx, 66110000, 72xxxxxx) across ME authorities, and it also carries private-sector buyer requests that never reach the state portal.

source_name: Posta Crne Gore - Javne nabavke (state postal operator procurement)
why_relevant: Posta Crne Gore runs the largest physical counter network in ME (~135 units) and provides cash/payment services; it is a contracting authority that publishes its own procurement page. Its notices for counter hardware, cash handling, printers/thermal rolls and payment terminals are a direct read on non-bank cash-and-payments infrastructure demand.

source_name: Elektroprivreda Crne Gore (EPCG) - Javne nabavke
why_relevant: Largest ME state-owned utility and a mass biller; its tenders for bill-payment collection, POS/kiosk payment acceptance, card-acquiring and cash-collection services indicate where retail payment volumes and terminal demand sit outside banks.

source_name: CBCG - Racun za placanje sa osnovnim uslugama (basic payment account)
why_relevant: Companion comparison set covering basic accounts and accounts for vulnerable consumers; discloses which banks offer them and at what card/ATM fee levels - a financial-inclusion and cash-access signal.

source_name: CBCG - Zastita prava klijenata kreditnih institucija i korisnika finansijskih usluga (consumer complaints function)
why_relevant: The CBCG consumer-protection service handles complaints against banks, payment institutions, MFIs and leasing companies. Complaint statistics and thematic reports expose recurring failure modes in cards, ATM withdrawals, POS/e-commerce chargebacks and fees - weak signals of terminal-estate quality and where providers are under pressure.

source_name: Zavod za zaposljavanje Crne Gore (ZZZCG) - oglasi o slobodnim radnim mjestima
why_relevant: The national employment agency's vacancy register carries statutory job postings from banks and PSPs. Ads naming card platforms, ATM maintenance, 'kartichno poslovanje', 'monitoring bankomata', switch/authorisation systems reveal which institutions are building or replacing card/ATM capability - the core weak signal where private-bank procurement is invisible.

source_name: Bankar.me - Oglasi za posao (banking job-ads section)
why_relevant: Specialist ME banking portal that republishes bank recruitment ads (Prva banka, CKB, Komercijalna, CBCG) with full role descriptions - including payment-operations and card-business roles. Pre-filtered to the sector, so far higher signal density than general job boards, and it timestamps hiring waves that precede platform projects.

source_name: Zaposli.ME - IT job listings (Montenegro)
why_relevant: Described as the most-visited ME job board; its IT section carries bank and vendor postings naming concrete technologies (card management systems, ISO 8583, switch, ATM monitoring, Oracle/Java core-banking integrations). Technology names in ads are the cheapest available proxy for which platforms are installed at ME banks and processors.
